work_items.closure_criterion: Single source of truth: update this register with each checkpoint; no undocumented new roadmap or silent closeout.
Reconcile canonical source paths, recent implementation closeouts, live proof and explicit deferrals; retain unverified states.
Recover CL-DS-001 v1.3.0 from authoritative source; inspect before imposing design changes; record if unavailable.
Freeze 1.0 minimum workflows; approvals required for risky downgrades, disabling protections and deferrals of mandatory functions.
End-to-end Library explorer, versions, records, collection-sharing, folder permissions, copy/move/archive, server-side matching bulk selection, privacy and stale grants.
Implement dynamic legal-hold/retention propagation to future descendants where in-scope; verify ancestor checks cannot be bypassed by rename/move/trash.
Only enable physical/provider file destruction after generation-fenced delete, legal/hold checks, independent review, real provider failure-injection and recovery proof; until then disable it.
Verify S3/NAS/local upload provider reconciliation, lease and object identity under interrupted multipart finalization, revocation and concurrent cleanup; no physical deletion on ambiguous ownership.
Safe version-pinned PDF/image/audio/video review derivatives, exact recipient authorization, approved vs changes-requested decision, provenance and revoked-reviewer behavior.
Watermark settings, manual/default rules, immutable delivery provenance, privacy-safe image/PDF/media rendering, metadata stripping and recipient-specific revocation.
Packet publishing, acknowledgements, expiry, reminder/overdue evidence, signed manifest integrity, large roster pagination; live non-admin recipient, no underlying Library source access.
One durable Transfer Center for upload/download/import/export: streaming, resume, pause, cancel, retries, checksums, bounded RAM/disk and truthful progress.

source_progress_notes: Pass 3 guards observational transfer inspection, file/checkpoint snapshot identity and transfer/MSI lock cleanup. Original closeout criteria remain open.

Pass 5: native archive appends persist schema-2 SHA256 streaming state; bounded tail/timestamp check per chunk; full-file inspect/commit/stage verification remains authoritative; explicit full-hash repair. Qt helper-per-384-KiB-chunk cost and broader Transfer Center remain open.

Pass 6: Desktop native archive segments raised from bounded 384 KiB to 512 KiB to reduce short-lived helper invocations; Qt validates full evidence then redacts private schema-2 streaming SHA-256 state/tail/disk timestamp. Still no persistent session and not Qt/Windows certified.
Pass 7: read-only native diagnosis differentiates malformed streaming-hash state from invalid core checkpoint metadata; result is unverified and requires explicit complete-byte recovery to repair.

Pass 9: operator-confirmed native recovery can verify committed archive after pending checkpoint crash; ordinary reads still fenced, tampered archive retains evidence. Source tests only; broad Transfer Center and Windows runtime acceptance remain open.

G26 Pass 10 reconciliation: recovered and integrated the verified Qt download continuity (strict Range/If-Range, ETag, length, destination safety), per-scope single-writer queue (standby read-only, manual resumption), and canonical /api/uploads session protocol; fixed first-profile queue directory initialization before QLockFile acquisition. Executable portable C++ range tests, Qt source contracts, native Go tests/race/cross-compile passed; live Qt/Windows tests still open.

G26 P11: native Qt HTTP Range admission prevents automatic excessive tiny-fragment continuation on large downloads; preserves last short fragment. 56 executable/source range assertions, desktop contract checks; Qt/Win10 untested.

G26 Pass 12: Desktop Qt queue destination collision prevention, oldest-terminal-only journal retention and safe admission cap, atomic new-job persistence, malformed journal read-only hold, and volatile per-readyRead progress; Qt/Windows runtime still unverified.

G26 Pass 13: Redacted, read-only journal health capability and separate UI error/ownership states; no silent empty queue or unsafe takeover on invalid data. Qt Windows runtime and manual recovery acceptance remain open.

G26 Pass 14: post-admission QSaveFile failures force a distinct native write hold, abort network work, preserve bytes/previous committed state and require explicit reload plus manual resume. 32 source contracts plus inherited checks; live Qt/Win10 runtime and other-device parity not certified.

G26 Pass 15: native Qt transfer mutations now return committed-result bools and broker no longer reports updated:true after failed/disallowed per-transfer queue mutations. Retry All acknowledges possible partial success; 34/34 source contracts. No Qt/Windows acceptance.

G26 Pass 16: two-phase Desktop download completion stores SHA256 commit intent before rename, then final receipt; explicit resume re-hashes the retained partial or final file after an interrupted rename/save, rejects ambiguous/corrupt evidence. 28 source assertions; no linked Qt/Win10 certification.
Pass 17: native Desktop queue journal validates records and protected automatic cleanup; untrusted or oversized journal is held.

Pass 18: native Broker now admits authenticated same-server viewer downloads and opaque-handle project file uploads, with canonical server finalization and session-path controls. Related-work attachment links remain explicitly blocked.

Pass 19: Downloads now write explicit zero unknown total so strict journal can reload them; uploads pin size/mtime and refuse changed/unpinned source sessions; unexpected saved destinations cannot execute file writes/renames/open. Historical evidence retained; real OS handle identity and Qt/Windows/browser/mobile behavior remain unverified.

Pass 20: before consuming verified upload via Project-file finalization, Desktop saves an immutable session/checksum/length intent; retry after lost finalization reply replays only the original authorized idempotent finalizer and validates the server asset response, not the consumed upload session. Native Qt runtime certification remains outstanding.

Pass 21: native transfer finalizes Project asset and independently attaches evidence relationship; durable link intent and verified receipt allow retry without source reupload. Pass 22: strict recovered relationship receipts, server deduplicated identity/audit, distinct UI stages, retained canceled-link evidence, and native push snapshot consumption. Live acceptance remains open.

work_items.source_implemented: partial: Pass44 adds separately authorized, default-disabled native supervised MSI rollback with a durable non-replayable journal while preserving the original install receipt and completed upgrade journal. No replay/clearance authority. Pass48: bounded same-file/mode/size/timestamp-preserving receipt rewrite defense: SHA-256 content snapshots before and after full profile inspection for both attempt and lifecycle files. No new mutation authority. Pass49: bounded profile-wide read-only incident inventory includes orphan upgrade/repair/uninstall/rollback journals, stable receipt hashes, original registration observation and non-replay operator actions; no journal clearance or executable remediation. Pass50: exclusive nonce-keyed one-use grant and MSI lifecycle/attempt/lock custody now synchronizes parent directories where supported and validates published grant entry identity; Windows power-loss remains unverified.

source_progress_notes: Pass 3 guards observational transfer inspection, file/checkpoint snapshot identity and transfer/MSI lock cleanup. Original closeout criteria remain open.
MSI child is Job-assigned before resumption; external Windows Installer service/custom actions, post-reboot attestation, update/repair/uninstall are not certified. Source progress only.
Pass 23 verifies read-only local MSI history before grant, blocks duplicate or unexplained attempts, and fences view changes. No OS-backed repair/reinstall or healthy installed-state proof.

Pass24 refuses existing/ambiguous MSI ProductCodes and cross-Package custody collisions before one-use grant consumption. No silent update/repair/retry; OS verification and real Windows runtime still open.

Pass25 serializes Package-key MSI attempts with a profile-wide atomic lock across receipt custody scan, grant consumption, and msiexec outcome; orphan lock exposed for manual review, no automatic clearing/retry.
Pass26 enumerates a bounded, fail-closed local MSI history/locks per private profile; Qt and Desktop validate evidence independently, without clear/retry/upgrade authority.

Pass27 requires completed MSI enumeration of current-user+machine contexts and re-probes after the durable prepared receipt, before msiexec. Unknown custody files/ambiguous product states fail closed; other-user contexts and live installer health remain outside coverage.

Pass28 double-samples bounded read-only MSI inventory and refuses receipt/lock mutations, replaced identities, and global admission changes during read. Snapshot remains observational, not an atomic transaction or installer health proof.

Pass34 holds and rehashes the exact Windows MSI open handle across execution, denies concurrent write/delete sharing, and revalidates ProductCode twice immediately before suspended-child resume; no global OS atomicity or automatic repair authority.

Pass35 source contract differentiates signed selected content from MSI-installed prerequisites. Go enforces live exact registration plus retained receipt digest and verifies it again before process resume; recovery surfaces bounded read-only known-dependency edges. No lifecycle mutation has been authorized and no Windows-installed application health is certified.

Pass36 adds read-only per-Package upgrade/repair/uninstall blocker projections, known dependent list and independent Go/Qt/renderer evidence validation. No separately signed lifecycle mutation authority or executor exists yet.

Pass37 adds separately signed default-off repair grants, exact prior receipt SHA, current-user registration/dependency rechecks before Job-supervised msiexec /fomus, and a crash-retained no-replay repair journal. Still NOT a release-ready repair feature or complete package lifecycle.

Pass38 adds signed admin-opt-in MSI uninstall with no-known-dependents and user registration admission, fixed msiexec /x ProductCode and a crash-retained shared lifecycle journal; no unattended replay, global OS dependency proof or automatic rollback. Certification not claimed.

Pass40 adds native signed read-only upgrade inspection requiring same ProductCode and increasing same-major MSI version, coherent profile/registration and a retained original MSI matching its receipt. Desktop and Qt expose review only; no signed upgrade execution or rollback permissions exist.

Pass41 signs upgrade-only scope with both predecessor receipt and MSI hashes and opts in administrator grant issuance. API explicitly marks nonexecutable. No upgrade native executor, rollback journal or Windows certification has been implemented.

Pass42 implements signed, default-off, non-replayable supervised MSI upgrade. The original receipt/retained MSI and successor stage are reverified under frozen Windows handles, crash journal is durable before grant consumption, and Windows registration recovery is observational only. No automatic rollback, dependent ordering proof, Windows OS health or certification.
